subject: how to specify initial value in a hierarchical model

messages.author: d1bdd751691ae3d0
messages.subject: how to specify initial value in a hierarchical model
parts:
I wanted to fit the parameters of the prospect theory. I used rstan to estimate the hyper-parameters. 

My model code and data are attached. There are 4 parameters, alpha, beta, lambda, and mu, My hypothesis was each parameter with a boundary, 

alpha and beta are both from 0 to 2, lambda is from 0 to 5, mu is from 0 to 50. each parameter is transformed from a parameter obeys a beta distribution 

with their own hyper-parameters theta1 and theta2.

I found that when I set init="0", and the 0<=mu<=10, there was no errors.

But there were still some errors in the sampling when I set the init="random" or set 0<=mu<=50.

The error messages like below,

 SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'prospectedtheory' NOW (CHAIN 1).
[1] "Error : Rejecting initial value:"                              
[2] "  Log probability evaluates to log(0), i.e. negative infinity."
[3] "  Stan can't start sampling from this initial value."          
[1] "error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done"

I don't know what's wrong with my model code or the initial value.

How can I check the code or set an initial value?

Thanks,
Lily

messages.author: 9b1ba46046eac99f
messages.subject: Re: how to specify initial value in a hierarchical model
parts:
Hi Lily,

it seems like sometimes, the 'u' value is too large or too small. You can try to print the variable by using the print() function.

Anyways, there are several places you could modify/improve. 

(1)
instead of using:
          pchoice <- inv_logit(mu[ID]*u);
          choice[ID, t] ~ bernoulli(pchoice);
try: 
          choice[ID, t] ~ bernoulli_logit(mu[ID]*u);

(2)
instead of declaring:
          for (i in 1:N) {
              alpha[i]     <- 2 * alpha_p[i];
try vectorizing it:
          alpha     <- 2 * alpha_p;

(3)
when assigning a negative value, please leave a space.
Do: 
          us[j] <-  (-lambda[ID]) * pow((-vs[j]), beta[ID]);
instead of :
          us[j] <-(-lambda[ID]) * pow((-vs[j]), beta[ID]);
 
(4) 
you could follow Stan Reference (2.9, P174) to reparameterize the prior of your beta distribution. 

Hope this helps.

L.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: how to specify initial value in a hierarchical model
parts:
> On Jul 25, 2016, at 10:38 AM, Lei Zhang <bnuzhan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Lily,
>
> it seems like sometimes, the 'u' value is too large or too small. You can try to print the variable by using the print() function.
>
> Anyways, there are several places you could modify/improve.
>
> (1)
> instead of using:
> pchoice <- inv_logit(mu[ID]*u);
> choice[ID, t] ~ bernoulli(pchoice);
> try:
> choice[ID, t] ~ bernoulli_logit(mu[ID]*u);
This won't affect efficiency, so it's more a matter of style.

>
> (2)
> instead of declaring:
> for (i in 1:N) {
> alpha[i] <- 2 * alpha_p[i];
> try vectorizing it:
> alpha <- 2 * alpha_p;

This one's all good. Vectorizing is more efficient and I think
the code's clearer.

>
> (3)
> when assigning a negative value, please leave a space.
> Do:
> us[j] <- (-lambda[ID]) * pow((-vs[j]), beta[ID]);
> instead of :
> us[j] <-(-lambda[ID]) * pow((-vs[j]), beta[ID]);

You don't need the first set of parens, so I'd just use this:

us[j] = -lambda[ID] * (-vs[j])^beta[ID];

vs[j] will have to be negative here or the answers aren't going
to make sense.

But I'm worried that you're using an index ID that's not
part of the left-hand side.

- Bob
